newsitem.title: FRANCE: Louis Harris poll shows left gaining in France.
newsitem.headline: Louis Harris poll shows left gaining in France.

text.p: Following are the results of an opinion poll of French voters' intentions ahead of the May 25/June 1 parliamentary election.
The telephone poll of 1,003 adults aged 18 and over was conducted by Louis Harris on May 2 and 3 for LCI television and weekly Politique Opinion and made public on May 5. It gave no seat projections.

Louis Harris said 18 percent of those polled did not say how they would vote. It said the voting intentions were based on responses from the 883 people who said they were both registered and would definitely vote.

The poll also showed 45 percent would prefer the Socialists and Communists to hold a majority in the National Assembly, a three percentage point increase since the previous Harris poll conducted on April 25 and 26. Support for a ruling centre-right majority was unchanged at 43 percent.
However, 63 percent said a win for the centre-right was the most likely outcome, with 21 percent expecting the Socialists and Communists to secure a majority.
The poll showed 22 percent of those surveyed thought Socialist Party leader Lionel Jospin had staged the best electoral campaign, the best performance among the five main party leaders.

RPR leader Alain Juppe came second with 13 percent, UDF leader Francois Leotard tied with Communist head Robert Hue on eight percent while National Front leader Jean-Marie Le Pen scored seven. Forty-two percent gave no view.
